# @game-studio/arcade-base

## Installation
```
$ npm install @game-studio/arcade-base --save
```
> :warning: **You should not install any of the other @game-studio packages as they are within the arcadee-base and initialised / version controled through that.**

You will also need to install the following as they are peer dependencies of this package:
```js
"@esotericsoftware/spine-pixi-v8": "4.x.x",
"howler": "2.x.x",
"inversify": "5.x.x",
"pixi.js": "8.x.x",
"vue": "2.x.x"
```

## Usage
### Step 1: Config
The config should follow the IEngineConfig interface. You can look at that interface definition to see what items it requires with descriptions [here](./src/config-model.ts)

### Step 2: Create the required components
Each game will need to implement the following components matching the specified interfaces then bind them in the ContainerModule (described below).

Here is a list of those components and interfaces (click the links for more details and basic implmentations).
- [GameModel<implement IBaseGameModel>](./wiki/injectable-components/game-model.md)
- [GameSettings<implement IBaseGameSettingsModel>](./wiki/injectable-components/game-settings.md)
- [DebugModel<implement IBaseDebugModel>](./wiki/injectable-components/debug-model.md)
- [GameApplication<implement IGameApp>](./wiki/injectable-components/game-application.md)
- [CoreDataList<implement IAssetConfig>](./wiki/injectable-components/core-data-list.md)
- [Cabinet<extend CabinetPackage>](./wiki/injectable-components/cabinet.md)
- [Skin<implement ISkinDesc>](./wiki/injectable-components/skin-description.md)

### Step 3: Define a Container Module
Now you can bind all these components ready for the game to run:

See the [bindings section](./wiki/bindings.md) for more details
```ts
// file bindings.ts

import { ContainerModule } from 'inversify';
import { BaseCabinet, BigWin, container, Injects, IAssetConfig, IGameApp, ISkinDesc } from '@arcade-client/base-package';

export const containerModule = new ContainerModule((bind, __, ___, rebind) => {
    bind<IBaseDataList>(Injects.CoreDataList).toConstantValue(coreDataList);
    bind<GameModel>(Injects.GameModel).toConstantValue(new GameModel);
    bind<GameSettings>(Injects.GameSettings).toConstantValue(new GameSettings);
    bind<DebugModel>(Injects.DebugModel).toConstantValue(new DebugModel);
    bind<IGameApp>(Injects.GameApp).toConstantValue(new GameApplication());

    bind<() => void>(Injects.SkinFactory).toFactory(() => {
        return async () => {
            const skinName = container.frameConnection.parentConstants.currentSkin;
            const { skinDescription } = await import(`@/src/skins/${skinName}`);
            bind<ISkinDesc>(Injects.Skin).toConstantValue(skinDescription);
        };
    });

    bind<() => void>(Injects.ComponentsFactory).toFactory(() => {
        return () => {
            bind<BaseCabinet>(Injects.Cabinet).toConstantValue(new BaseCabinet());
            bind<BigWin>(Injects.BigWin).toConstantValue(new BigWin());
            // this binding is technically optional if you don't want a bigwin popup just don't bind anything to this
        };
    });
});
```

### Step 4: Initialising the package
Finally create an instance of the basePackage and call initialise() passing in your defined Config and ContainerModule.
```ts
    const basePackage = new BaseGame();
    basePackage.initialise(engineConfig, containerModule);
```

## Other Features
### Initialisation Execution Order
A breakdown of the order components initialise within the package is available here
* [Order of Execution](./wiki/setup-order-of-execution.md)

### Feature Toggles
Makes use of the feature-control package for easy access to featureToggles defined in the AdminPanel.
FeatureToggles are loaded during the Bootstrap process (See [Order of Execution](./wiki/setup-order-of-execution.md) for specific timing) and can be access, as below, after that.
```ts
import { FeatureToggles } from '@arcade-client/base-package';

FeatureToggles.getKey('Arcade_App_Cabinet_Autobuy_IsLive')
```

### Events
All the events are commented with when they fire (or should be fired by the game) and those comments are visible in intellisense when developing for ease of use.

Head to the [events file](../src/services/events.ts) to see all the events and their descriptions.

### Asset Management:
> :warning: **Import the assetManager from base-package - do not add @arcade-cient/asset-manager as a dependency directly.

Asset lists are loaded from the cdn via the CoreDataList and SkinDataList components defined by the game.

They are typically stored in the root of each asset version folder, see example CDN structure below.

#### Asset Quality Support
Dynamic asset qualities are supported via the AssetQualityGetter Inject. That can be bound to a function which returns a string for the desired quality. It will be called just before assets are loaded, so after the Device and frameConnections have been established if you wish to use those to determine the quality.

Within assetLists the {quality} tag can be used in place of the quality folder in file paths and the basePackage will swap that to the specified quality string at run time.

#### Device Dependant Asset Support
The interface ICdnAssetConfig has been provided which can be used to structure your AssetLists. It extends IAssetConfig to add a DeviceDependantAssets property which the basePackage checks to load any assets that are only needed on either mobile or desktop devices.
```ts
export interface ICdnAssetConfig extends IAssetConfig {
    baseUrl: string;
    fontUrl?: string;
    assetList: IAssetList;
    skin: string;
    version: string;
    deviceDependantAssets?: {
        mobile: IAssetList;
        desktop: IAssetList;
    };
}
```
#### Audio types
A note about audio types supported across browsers.

Modern browsers allow for a cascading file type (i.e. {ogg,mp3}) where they will use the first item in the list that is compatible.

:warning: **IE and Edge do not support this directly but the engine will replace {ogg,mp3} with just mp3 on those Browsers. Using any other combination of file types will not be replaced and could cause errors on those browsers.

Then update the above text appropriately.

#### Fonts
Fonts are different to other assets in that they should be stored in the static folder of the game Project and referenced in the fonts.css file at the same location, example below.

*woff is the preferred font format as its designed specifically for web and is better supported across browsers*
e.g.
```css
@font-face {
    font-family: 'Lato-Bold';
    src: url('./Lato-Bold.woff') format('woff');
}
```

#### Example CDN Structure
**Root Path:** *clients/mobile/arcade/assets/en_GB/*

There is a template assets folder on the cdn that can be copied for easy initial setup.

```
├── GAMENAME (e.g. spin or scratch)
│   ├── core
│   │   ├── CORE_VERSION (eg. ver-1.0.0 or js-0001)
│   │   │   ├── QUALITY (eg. 1 or 0.5)
│   │   │   │   ├── game-rules
│   │   │   ├── asset-list.json
│   │   │   ├── strings.json (if not mnually binding strings)
│   ├── SKIN_NAME (e.g. classic or cosmos)
│   │   ├── SKIN_VERSION
│   │   │   ├── QUALITY (eg. 1 or 0.5)
│   │   │   │   ├── game-rules
│   │   │   ├── asset-list.json
```

### EndGameValidation
The EndGameValidator package is used here. `startGame`, `continueGame` and `reset` are all automatically called by the package. `endGame` is called inside the BaseCabinet.endGame function which you'll need to manually call when the game ends.

- `startGame` is called during the resume if GameComplete is false.
It is also called on any successful Begin request.
- `continueGame` is called on any successful Continue request

You will need to create any Validators implementing IValidator and add them to the validator like so:
```ts
// SomeValidator.ts
// Define your custom Validator
export class SomeValidator implements IValidator {
    public isValid(message: ISpinServerResponse): boolean {
        // perform some kind of check against the `message` to ensure the player see the correct information
        // return true if correct false if any discrepencies are found
        return false;
    }
    
    public getError(message: ISpinServerResponse): string {
        let errorMessage: string = '';
        // construct your error message here detailing what was found that didn't match the server data.
        return 'errorMessage';
    }
}

// Some other file
// Be sure to add it to the validator system like so
endGameValidator.addItemToValidate(new ReelValidator(this));
```

## Development
While working on this you should make use of `npm link` to link your local version to the game you are working with as follows:

**Step 1: Establish the link**
- While in the base-package folder run the following command: `npm link`
- Go to your Game project and do the following in the specific games folder: `npm link @arcade-client/base-package`
- *The projects are now linked together via a sym-link meaning the folder in game/node_modules/base-package is a copy of mono-repo/package/base-package.*
- You can now build the game as normal with: `npm run dev`

**Step 2: Applying changes**
- You can now make changes to the base-package code in your mono-repo folder and save them as normal.
- Then, still in the base-package, build those changes with: `npm run build`
- When the build is complete, you'll see your game project automatically rebuild itself if linked correctly.
- Also when the build is complete you may need to scroll up in the terminal winodw to see any errors, if you get to a big green section the build was successful.

### WebPack bundle
To check the bundle created by web-pack to see exactly what has been bundled
```
npm run build-stats
npm run analyze
```
> :warning: For some reason after running `npm run build-stats` the resulting stats.json file is created with a line at the top making the json invalid so npm run analyze fails to read it. I've been manually removing this line to get around that issue for now.

This uses "webpack-bundle-analyzer" to display a page breaking down the contents of the bundle.

### Linting
```
npm run lint
```

Runs `tslint` and outputs any errors.

### Publishing
> :warning: This package should not be published manually. Publishing is handled by the parent [arcade-client-monorepo](https://github.com/tombolaltd/arcade-client-monorepo) using lerna.

**Note:** it's worth noting that the private registry the package is published to is defined in the `package.json` file.
